note: v1 97.58 (seeds 0/11 97.58/97.50), Quarter to Sixteen: a modern jazz-funk big band in 15/16 (4+4+4+3), the bar a sixteenth short so the one keeps arriving early. Synth bass and clav lock with a ghost-note tight kit; rootless m9 chords plane in parallel, a new one every bar; a horn theme in Ab Dorian (brass, saxes a fifth below) whose second phrase answers a fourth up; a quiet 7/8 bridge on vibes a key away; a synth-lead solo that goes from long notes to sixteenths, with swelling sax pads behind; a shout chorus of horn hits sliding a sixteenth later every bar; out-theme and a one-hit tag. Draft 95.5 -> 97.6: highs cut at 4 kHz, a quieter bridge.

v2 97.02 kept on judgment (seeds 0/11 97.02/96.97 vs v1 97.58/97.50): a DRUM BREAK before the shout chorus, the big-band set-up the song lacked. Six bars of kit alone (the bass hits each one) regroup the 15 bar by bar: the groove's bones with a three-tom pick-up, accents every 5 sixteenths (5+5+5), every 3 (3x5), 5s and 3s again, then a sixteenth roll down the toms into the shout's crash. compscore's variety reads it as less timbre spread (-0.5), not a break in the song; a 4-bar version scored 96.98/96.88.

v3 97.05 (seeds 0/11 97.05/97.02 vs v2 97.02/96.97): the out-theme becomes CALL AND RESPONSE - the brass take the even bars, the saxes answer on the odd ones a fourth lower, and they come together for the last two bars. Those two bars are doubled on a new GLITCH track, a horn section through wM's fixed stutter (1/16 slices, 3 repeats, chance .5), so the horns' last word stutters before the one-hit tag.

v4 97.28 (seeds 0/11 97.28/96.83 vs v3 97.05/97.02): the synth solo SINGS and the bass leads into the bridge. The solo's opening long notes are now scooped into from a whole step below, a sixteenth grace that the mono lead's glide (opened to 80 ms) turns into a bend up, and each phrase's last note falls back a half step. The last theme bar ends in a sixteenth BASS FILL down the Dorian (Ab Gb F Eb Db B Bb), landing a tritone away from the bridge's E so the key change arrives through a side door.
